chunks: Except from their wives and those whom their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy.

key_terms.مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ: those whom their right hands possess (concubines/slaves)

ai.seo_question: Who are the permissible partners for men according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Mu'minun is often interpreted alongside its counterpart in Surah An-Nur to establish the primary categories of lawful intimacy, with scholars like Al-Tabarsi emphasizing the term 'ghayr maluminin' (not blameworthy) as a divine guarantee of purity within these bounds. The inclusion of 'what their right hands possess' reflects the historical context of concubinage, which Shia jurists analyze in relation to marriage contracts and offspring legitimacy, distinguishing it from the permanent status of wives.
